BAS.MY Johor Bahru: observed vs scheduled bus service

KD44103 Big Data Analytics · Group G12 · Phase 3 results dashboard

24 November 2026

8,572GPS records from 103 realtime snapshots
2,801stop arrivals inferred by Spark
28%arrivals on time (−1 to +5 min)
41%arrivals more than 1 min early
n/ascheduled trips seen in the feed

Research question. How do the buses we can actually see moving (GPS, GTFS-Realtime) compare with the published BAS.MY timetable (static GTFS)? Data window: 2026-11-24 14:31:55 to 2026-11-24 15:27:55 (1 day(s), 2.9 MB raw JSON).

Pipeline

Stage Tool What happens
Ingest Python collector polls the GTFS-Realtime API every 30 s, decodes protobuf → JSON Lines, partitions by date
Store SQLite (SQL) + Parquet keyed relational schema for the timetable + Spark outputs; views and report queries in sql/
Process Apache Spark (PySpark, Spark SQL) flatten nested JSON, clean, GPS pairs → speeds, stop-arrival inference, headways, 250 m grid
Model Spark MLlib + R delay regression (5 algorithms), grid clustering (4 algorithms), Wilcoxon tests
Present R ggplot2 / R Markdown this dashboard and the report figures
Data-quality step Count
snapshots (feed versions) 103
vehicle records (raw) 8,572
records with no trip_id 0
records with trip_id not in GTFS 0
records outside Johor bbox 0
duplicate (vehicle, timestamp) 0
clean vehicle records 8,572
distinct vehicles 130
distinct trips observed 155
distinct routes observed 19

Objective 1 · Speed by route and hour

Measured over all observed routes, buses move at 28.6 km/h against 24.8 km/h implied by the timetable. 11 of 19 routes run faster than scheduled, and 8 run slower.

The best model is Random forest (Spark MLlib) (RMSE 4.60 min, R² 0.94), against 19.61 min for the training-mean baseline.

Limitations

  • Arrivals are inferred from 30-second GPS fixes (interpolated where the track passes within 60 m of a stop), not recorded.
  • Routes or buses missing from the feed cannot be assessed; a missing trip may be a tracking gap rather than a cancellation.
  • The timetable has a 1-minute resolution, and every trip uses the ALLDAY service, so it does not change for peak hours or weekends.
